guide: Start here: open Start and type the household name, the two partner names, the savings rate you want, the car limit and the monthly amount for big purchases in the yellow cells.
Replace demo data, step 1: clear the demo rows of Big purchases, Purchase options, Move plan, Event budget, Tax documents and Deduction records and type your own; keep the header rows.
Replace demo data, step 2: paste your monthly totals into Year by month and your category totals into Category changes, then type your own changes in the Next-year plan.
Replace demo data, step 3: type your own numbers in Rent or buy inputs and your own estimated payment dates in Estimated payments; your tax office gives you the dates.
Pay-day routine: when a freelance payment arrives, add it to Tax set-aside with the amount you moved; when you pay something for the tax return, add a Deduction record and keep the receipt.
Month-close routine, in this order: add the month to Year by month, read Missing receipts, read Missing documents, run the Set-aside Check and update the saved amount of each big purchase.
Run the Car Purchase Decision before you say yes to a car and the Purchase Order when two purchases compete for the same savings; any range shown is a typical range, check your own numbers.
A single adult with one income and no children can use the purchase, tax and year sheets: leave the partner 2 and children rows empty and use Partner 1 as the person.
Use the 18 tools for the big decisions, print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details written in.
Read the dashboard and the Charts page before the tax date and at the year end: purchases, documents, receipts, set-aside and the year review.

Why a workbook: one flat price, no yearly renewal, your data stays with you and there is nothing to link or re-connect; you type or paste your own data. It works in Excel and Google Sheets with no macros.
What this is not: it is not a bank app, and not tax, legal, investment or credit advice; check your local rules and ask your adviser. Every verdict is an estimate from your numbers.

listing.title: Big Purchases, Tax Papers and Year Review Excel Template: Car Decision, Moving Plan, Tax Checklist, Deduction Records, Year in Review
listing.headline: Decide the big purchases, keep the tax papers and review the year
listing.description:
Decide the big, rare money questions of your household in one Excel workbook, for a single adult, a couple or a family. The Car Purchase Decision tests price, deposit, trade-in, loan term, rate and running cost and shows the monthly cost, the total over the years you keep the car and its share of take-home pay against your own limit. Each car option is tested at six loan terms side by side. The Purchase Order shows which big purchase to fund first when the car and a move compete for the same savings, and the Moving Plan lists every move cost with the cash needed month by month and the date you have it.

The Rent or Buy comparison uses your own typed numbers over 15 years and marks the year buying starts to cost less. It is an estimate from your numbers, never advice. An event budget tracks estimates, deposits and what is paid against a target.

The tax pages keep your papers in order: a Tax Documents Checklist with received and filed dates and a countdown to the due date your tax office gave you, a Missing Documents list ranked by days overdue, Deduction Records with receipts kept and missing by category, a Missing Receipts list ranked by amount, and a Tax Set-aside with a running balance checked against the next estimated payment. Nothing here says what is claimable: check your local rules and ask your adviser.

The Year Review sets the last 12 complete months against the 12 before: income, spending, saving rate, debt paid, interest paid, net worth change, goals and loans reached and the biggest category changes. The Next-year Plan starts from last year's actuals with a typed change per category, shown a month and for each paycheck.

18 decision tools, 12 printable sheets, 12 documents, 12 checklists and 34 ready text messages come with it. This is part eight of the Household Finance suite. A standard .xlsx workbook that works in Excel and Google Sheets, with no macros, no subscription and no bank links: you type or paste your own data. The demo copy is full of sample data. It is a household money kit, not a bank app, and not tax, legal, investment or credit advice.

Received on {col:set_aside.date} from {col:set_aside.source}: {col:set_aside.amount}. Moved to the set-aside: {col:set_aside.moved}. Suggested by the percentage in Settings: {col:set_aside.suggested}.
Running balance after the estimated payments made so far: {col:set_aside.balance}.
The percentage is an estimate: confirm it with your adviser.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own household.

documents.title: Tax papers pack for the tax preparer
paragraphs: Tax papers pack of {set:household} for tax year {col:tax_docs.tax_year}, dated {today}.
Documents in hand: {col:tax_docs.received_count} of {col:tax_docs.year_total}. Overdue: {col:tax_docs.missing_count}. Due date: {col:tax_docs.due_date}.

Deduction records for the year: {col:tax_docs.year_deductions}, receipts missing: {col:tax_docs.receipts_missing}. Childcare recorded: {col:tax_docs.childcare_total}. Tax set-aside balance: {col:tax_docs.set_balance}.
Please tell us if you need anything else for the year.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own household.

documents.title: Year review, one line
paragraphs: Year review of {set:household}, dated {today}. Item: {col:year_review.item}.
Last 12 months: {col:year_review.this_year}. The 12 months before: {col:year_review.last_year}. Change: {col:year_review.change} ({col:year_review.change_pct}), {col:year_review.note}.
Savings rate over the last 12 months: {col:year_review.savings_rate_all}. Net worth change: {col:year_review.nw_change_all}.
Both periods are complete months, so the comparison is fair. Estimates from your own numbers.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own household.

documents.title: Next-year plan, one category
paragraphs: Next-year plan of {set:household}, dated {today}. Category: {col:next_year_plan.category} ({col:next_year_plan.group}).
Last 12 months: {col:next_year_plan.last_year}. Change you typed: {col:next_year_plan.change}. Plan for next year: {col:next_year_plan.plan}, which is {col:next_year_plan.diff} against last year.
That is {col:next_year_plan.per_month} a month and {col:next_year_plan.per_paycheck} for each paycheck. The whole plan is {col:next_year_plan.plan_total}.
An estimate from your numbers: change it as the year goes on.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own household.
